title: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy generation is on by default — CEL validate rules become API-server policies

detection.reason: which policies qualify for generation is decided by Kyverno

remediation: Expect Kyverno to create ValidatingAdmissionPolicies (+ bindings) for policies whose validate rules are pure CEL; the API server then enforces them even while Kyverno is down. Turn it off with the admission controller's `--generateValidatingAdmissionPolicy=false` if you do not want that.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.rules[]?.validate?; .cel != null)) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row has a CEL validate rule
coversNotes: Chart kyverno changed: Enable the flag --generateValidatingAdmissionPolicy by default in the

title: CEL `image()` is renamed `parseImageReference()` — the old name stays as a deprecated alias
remediation: Replace `image(` with `parseImageReference(` in ValidatingPolicy / ImageValidatingPolicy expressions. The old name still compiles through 1.20 (`string_to_image_deprecated`, "alias for backward compatibility", kyverno/sdk at the v1.20.0 pin), so this is a deprecation to clear before the alias goes.
verifyCommand: kubectl get validatingpolicies.policies.kyverno.io,imagevalidatingpolicies.policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(tostring | test("[^A-Za-z_.]image[(]")) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row calls image()

title: A CEL validate rule can no longer use `context`, and `celPreconditions` need `validate.cel`
remediation: Remove `context` from rules that validate with CEL, and drop `celPreconditions` from rules that do not use `validate.cel`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.rules[]?; (.validate.cel != null and .context != null) or (.celPreconditions != null and .validate.cel == null))) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row combines them
coversNotes: v1.15.0 Fixed: Disabled context support when using CEL Expressions in

title: MutatingPolicies with CEL compilation errors are refused (1.15.2, 1.16.0)
quote: Fixed issue to block mutating policies upon compilation errors (#13972)
remediation: Fix MutatingPolicies whose CEL does not compile; they are refused on the next create/update.
verifyCommand: kubectl get mutatingpolicies.policies.kyverno.io -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select((.status.conditionStatus.ready // true) == false) | .metadata.name'  # each row is a MutatingPolicy Kyverno reports not ready

title: The chart's hook-Job images change — air-gapped mirrors need the image of the target version

detection.reason: registry mirrors live outside the cluster

remediation: The chart's Helm hook Jobs pull helper images that changed three times. The webhooks-cleanup image (`webhooksCleanup.image`, used by the pre-delete hooks) is `bitnami/kubectl` up to 1.14.4 and again on 1.15.0 (cut before the 1.14.5 backport), `alpine/kubectl` on 1.14.5, `registry.k8s.io/kubectl` from 1.15.1 and `ghcr.io/kyverno/readiness-checker` from 1.18.0; the post-upgrade report-cleanup hook (`policyReportsCleanup.image`) is `alpine/kubectl` on 1.14.5 and is gone from 1.15.1. Hooks run with the TARGET chart's values, so before an air-gapped upgrade mirror the image your target version uses (or pin your own with those values). On 1.14.4 or older the hooks still name `bitnami/kubectl` tags that are no longer published: the pre-delete hooks stall in ImagePullBackOff and `helm uninstall` hangs unless the image is overridden (seen with 1.13.6 on rtz-box) — and an upgrade TO 1.14.4 or 1.15.0 runs a post-upgrade hook with them.
verifyCommand: helm list -A -o json | jq -r '.[] | select(.chart | test("^kyverno-[0-9]")) | "\(.namespace)/\(.name) \(.chart) app \(.app_version)"'  # each row is a Kyverno Helm release; read its values with: helm get values NAME -n NAMESPACE

title: A namespaced Policy can no longer make an apiCall outside its own namespace (1.15.3, 1.16.3, 1.17.0)
quote: fix: prevent cross-namespace access in apiCall
remediation: In a namespaced `Policy` every context `apiCall.urlPath` must name the policy's own namespace: a path into another namespace, a path with no namespace segment (cluster-scoped resources, cluster-wide lists) and every `apiCall.service` call are refused ("path ... refers to namespace ..., which is different from the policy namespace", "path ... does not contain a namespace segment, which is required for namespaced policies"). There is no opt-out. Move such a rule into a ClusterPolicy scoped with `match.resources.namespaces`, or keep the lookup inside the policy's namespace. ClusterPolicies are not affected.
verifyCommand: kubectl get policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.namespace as $ns | select([.. | objects | .apiCall? // empty | objects] | any((.service != null) or ((.urlPath // "") | test("/namespaces/" + $ns + "(/|$)") | not))) | "Policy \($ns)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is a namespaced Policy whose apiCall calls a service or a path that does not literally name its own namespace (a path built from a variable is listed too: check what it resolves to)

title: A rule's context is capped at 2Mi by default (1.15.3, 1.16.3, 1.17.0)

detection.reason: the size of the data a rule loads is only known when it runs

remediation: ClusterPolicy / Policy rules that load more than 2Mi into their context (a cluster-wide `apiCall` list, a large ConfigMap or GlobalContextEntry) now fail with "context size limit exceeded: N bytes exceeds limit of N bytes". Narrow the call (a namespaced path, a `jmesPath` that keeps only what the rule reads) or raise the limit: key `maxContextSize` in the `kyverno` ConfigMap, chart value `config.maxContextSize` (a quantity; the string `"0"` disables the check — an unquoted 0 is dropped by the chart).
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select([.. | objects | .context? // empty | arrays | .[] | select(.apiCall != null or .globalReference != null or .configMap != null)] | .[0] != null) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row loads API, global-context or ConfigMap data into a rule context — the entries that can exceed the limit
